mainTopic: The laws of גילוי (uncovered food and drink a snake may have poisoned), how venom behaves, and the start of a list of three kinds of forbidden wine
overview: The גמרא finishes a ruling about soured wine: after a set time it no longer falls under גילוי or יין נסך, though the נהרדעי still worry about גילוי because a snake sometimes drinks it anyway. Next comes a list of items that are not subject to גילוי: fermenting wine, cress dishes, כותח הבבלי, steadily dripping water, and the opening of a fig. Some of these come with limits, such as the strict custom of the בני גולה, vinegar that keeps snakes away, and bite marks in the כותח. The fig ruling is matched to רבי אליעזר, who relies on 'שומר פתאים ה׳'. רב ספרא then teaches that venom sinks, spreads, or floats depending on the snake's age, and the גמרא explains that an old snake grows stronger in body but weaker in venom. Sinking venom explains why an uncovered barrel or melon stays forbidden even after nine people ate or drank safely. A ברייתא forbids using uncovered water for many other purposes. The גמרא clarifies how אחרים differ from the תנא קמא about washing, and explains why one may give such water to his own cat but not to a friend's. The amud ends as רבי יהודה בן בתירא begins listing three kinds of wine, starting with יין נסך, and the list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: After the set time, the soured wine is free of both concerns
steps.stepSummary: From the point just discussed and on, the wine is not subject to גילוי or to יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: From this point on, it is not subject to the rule of uncovered liquids, and it is not subject to the rule of יין נסך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling that started just before this section: once the wine has passed the time limit it was discussing, two concerns fall away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate laws are lifted at once. A snake is assumed not to drink this soured wine, so גילוי does not apply. The wine is also no longer treated as real wine for the ban on יין נסך.

keyTerms.meaning: A liquid left uncovered, which we fear a snake may have drunk from and poisoned
Wine poured to an idol (or touched by an idol worshipper), which is forbidden

phrases.english: From this point onward —
it is not subject to the rule of exposure,
and it is not subject to the rule of libation wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ruling that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the stated time, the soured wine is exempt from גילוי and יין נסך.

steps.title: The נהרדעי still worry about exposure
steps.stepSummary: The נהרדעי say that even after three days there is still a concern of גילוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The נהרדעי say: even after three days, we still worry about exposure.
steps.whatsHappening: A different group of scholars disagrees with half of the ruling from step 1. They keep the worry about גילוי even after three days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נהרדעי only argue about גילוי. They do not mention יין נסך, so that part of step 1 is not being challenged here.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of the city of Neharde'a
We are worried; we take the concern into account

phrases.english: And the scholars of Neharde'a say:
Even after three days
we are concerned about exposure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the גילוי part of step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after three days, גילוי still applies.

steps.title: Why are the נהרדעי worried?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the view of the נהרדעי.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the נהרדעי still worry. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 assumed snakes avoid this soured wine. The question asks what the נהרדעי know that would undo that assumption.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the נהרדעי still fear גילוי after three days

steps.title: Sometimes a snake drinks it anyway
steps.stepSummary: Sometimes it happens that a snake drinks even this wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes it happens that a snake drinks it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: snakes usually avoid this wine, but sometimes one drinks it anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נהרדעי agree that snakes normally do not drink soured wine. They still worry because it does happen now and then, and the risk is to a person's life.

phrases.english: Sometimes it happens that it drinks.
phrases.notes: The one drinking is a snake. The גמרא doesn't say so because the whole topic is snakes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A snake sometimes drinks even this wine, so the concern stays.

steps.title: Fermenting wine is free of exposure concerns for three days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that fermenting wine is not subject to גילוי, and that fermenting lasts three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: fermenting wine is not subject to the rule of exposure. How long does it ferment? Three days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that starts a list of foods and drinks that are not subject to גילוי. The first item is wine that is still fermenting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While wine is bubbling and fermenting, a snake is assumed to stay away from it. The ברייתא also sets a time limit: fermenting lasts three days, so the exemption lasts only that long.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: יַיִן תּוֹסֵס אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי,
phrases.english: Fermenting wine is not subject to exposure,
and how long is its fermentation?
Three days.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יַיִן תּוֹסֵס אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new list of items exempt from גילוי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fermenting wine, during its three days of fermentation, is exempt from גילוי.

steps.title: Cress dishes are exempt, but the Diaspora was strict
steps.stepSummary: שחלים are not subject to גילוי, but בני גולה had a custom to forbid them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cress dishes are not subject to the rule of exposure, but the people of the Diaspora had a custom to forbid them.
steps.whatsHappening: The list goes on: food made from שחלים (cress) is not subject to גילוי by the basic law. The בני גולה still treated it as forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels here. By the basic law the food is allowed, and on top of that there is a local custom to be strict.

keyTerms.meaning: Cress, a sharp plant used in dishes
They had a custom to treat them as forbidden

phrases.english: Cress is not subject to exposure,
but the people of the Diaspora had a custom to forbid them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the next item to the list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cress is exempt by law, but the Diaspora custom forbids it.

steps.title: The custom applies only to cress dishes without vinegar
steps.stepSummary: The strict custom is only for cress without vinegar, because vinegar keeps snakes away.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when there is no vinegar in them. But if there is vinegar in them, it drives the snakes away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the strict custom from step 6. It applies only when the cress dish has no vinegar in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar keeps snakes away, so a cress dish with vinegar carries no real risk. Even the בני גולה would not forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when (introduces a limit)
It drives them away (keeps the snakes off)

phrases.english: And we said this only
where there is no vinegar in them,
but if there is vinegar in them —
it repels them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the snakes. The vinegar keeps them away, so even the strict custom does not apply.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵית בְּהוּ חַלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the custom described in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The strict custom does not apply to cress dishes that contain vinegar.

steps.title: כותח הבבלי is exempt, but the Diaspora was strict
steps.stepSummary: כותח הבבלי is not subject to גילוי, but בני גולה forbade it by custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: כותח הבבלי is not subject to the rule of exposure, but the people of the Diaspora had a custom to forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: Another item joins the list: כותח הבבלי, a Babylonian dip. Like the cress in step 6, it is allowed by law but forbidden by custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as step 6: allowed by the basic law, with a strict custom added on top.

phrases.aramaic: כּוּתָּח הַבַּבְלִי אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי,
phrases.english: Babylonian kutach is not subject to exposure,
but the people of the Diaspora had a custom to forbid it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּתָּח הַבַּבְלִי אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the next item to the list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כותח is exempt by law, but the Diaspora custom forbids it.

steps.title: כותח with marks in it is a real concern
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשי says that if the כותח has little holes or marks, we do worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשי said: if it has marks in it, we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשי adds a limit to the ruling on כותח. If there are marks in it, there is a real worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually כותח is assumed safe. Marks in it could come from a snake's fangs, and that makes the worry real and not just a custom.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who adds a limit here
Holes or marks, like those from a bite

phrases.english: Rav Menashei said:
If it has marks in it —
we are concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְנַשֵּׁי: אִי אִית בֵּיהּ נִקּוּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the exemption for כותח in step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כותח with marks in it is a real concern.

steps.title: Dripping water is exempt from exposure concerns
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that water collected as it drips is not subject to גילוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of שמואל: dripping water is not subject to the rule of exposure.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling from שמואל: water that is dripping into a container is not subject to גילוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The constant dripping keeps snakes away, so no one fears they drank from it. The next step explains exactly what counts as dripping.

keyTerms.meaning: Dripping water, falling drop by drop

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said in the name of Shmuel:
Dripping water
is not subject to exposure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מֵי טִיף טִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another item exempt from גילוי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dripping water is exempt from גילוי.

steps.title: Only when the drops fall one right after another
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי limits שמואל's ruling to water that drips without a break.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: this is only when it drips drop right after drop.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי narrows the ruling in step 10. The exemption works only if the drops keep falling one after another without a gap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slow dripping with long breaks would give a snake a chance to drink. Only steady, continuous dripping keeps the water safe.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is only when (introduces a condition)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And that is only when it makes
drop right after drop, drop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a condition on step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dripping water is exempt only if the drops fall continuously.

steps.title: The opening of a fig is exempt from exposure concerns
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the opening of a fig is not subject to גילוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of שמואל: the opening of a fig is not subject to the rule of exposure.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ruling from שמואל: we do not worry that a snake bit into the opening of a fig.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think a fig's opening could hold snake venom. שמואל says we do not worry about this, and the next steps ask whose view this follows.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said in the name of Shmuel:

phrases.aramaic: פִּי תְאֵנָה אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי.
phrases.english: The mouth of a fig is not subject to exposure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: פִּי תְאֵנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ruling of שמואל on גילוי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The opening of a fig is exempt from גילוי.

steps.title: Whose view does this ruling follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא שמואל's fig ruling agrees with.
steps.simpleTranslation: In accordance with whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which earlier source supports שמואל's ruling about the fig. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being lenient about a real danger needs support. The גמרא wants to know which תנא would agree with such a lenient ruling.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא agrees with שמואל's ruling on the fig

steps.title: It follows רבי אליעזר: God protects the simple
steps.stepSummary: שמואל follows רבי אליעזר, who allows eating grapes and figs at night without worry, based on 'שומר פתאים ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like this תנא, as it was taught: רבי אליעזר says, a person may eat grapes and figs at night and need not worry, because it says: 'God protects the simple.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל follows רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר lets a person eat grapes and figs at night without worrying, even though he cannot see them well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At night you cannot check fruit for snake bites, yet רבי אליעזר still allows eating it. His reason is the פסוק 'שומר פתאים ה׳': in ordinary, everyday activities, God protects people. שמואל's leniency about the fig fits this approach.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period

steps.whatToRemember: Many items are exempt from גילוי because snakes avoid them, though some had strict customs or limits. שמואל's ruling about the fig follows רבי אליעזר, who relies on 'שומר פתאים ה׳': for ordinary risks that everyone takes, we do not have to worry.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'שומר פתאים ה׳' becomes an important general rule: for normal risks that everyone takes, a person may rely on Heaven's protection.

phrases.english: Like this tanna, as it was taught:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
A person may eat grapes and figs at night
and need not worry,
because it is said:
"The Lord protects the simple."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל follows רבי אליעזר, who relies on 'שומר פתאים ה׳'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אליעזר about eating fruit at night

steps.title: Three kinds of snake venom
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא, in the name of רבי יהושע דרומא, says venom behaves differently by the snake's age: a young snake's sinks, a middle-aged snake's spreads through, and an old snake's floats.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said in the name of רבי יהושע דרומא: There are three kinds of venom. A young snake's venom sinks, a middle-aged snake's venom spreads through the liquid, and an old snake's venom floats.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement teaches how snake venom behaves inside a liquid, depending on how old the snake is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is where the poison ends up after a snake drinks from uncovered liquid. If it sinks, the bottom is dangerous. If it floats, the top is dangerous. If it spreads, the whole thing is dangerous. This sets up the practical rules that come next.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ דָּרוֹמָא:
phrases.english: Rav Safra said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua of the South:
There are three kinds of venom:
that of a young snake sinks,
that of a middle-aged snake spreads through,
and that of an old snake floats.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ דָּרוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which items are subject to גילוי (steps 10-14) to how the venom itself behaves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Venom sinks, spreads, or floats depending on whether the snake is young, middle-aged, or old.

steps.title: Doesn't a snake get stronger with age?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that venom gets weaker as a snake ages, using a ברייתא that says a snake grows stronger as it gets older.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that the older a snake gets, the weaker it becomes? But a ברייתא teaches that three creatures grow stronger as they age: a fish, a snake, and a pig!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. רב ספרא's statement suggests old snakes are weaker, but a ברייתא says snakes get stronger with age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Floating venom is the weakest kind, since it doesn't go deep. So רב ספרא implies an old snake is weaker. The ברייתא says the opposite, so the two seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? (opens a question about what a statement implies)

phrases.english: Is this to say that the older it gets
the weaker its strength becomes?
But it was taught in a ברייתא:
Three creatures, the more they age,
the more strength is added to them,
and these are: a fish, a snake, and a pig!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what step 15 implies about old snakes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of רב ספרא's statement that an old snake's venom, which floats, is weaker.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says snakes grow stronger with age, which contradicts the idea that they weaken.

steps.title: Body gets stronger, venom gets weaker
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the snake's body strength grows with age, but its venom becomes weaker.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the snake's physical strength that increases, but its venom weakens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by showing the two sources talk about two different kinds of strength.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא means the snake's body gets stronger. רב ספרא means its venom gets weaker. Both can be true at once, so there is no contradiction.

phrases.english: It is its body strength that keeps increasing,
but its venom becomes weak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think 'stronger' means every kind of strength, venom included.
steps.terutzMaskana: Body strength grows with age while venom strength fades, so both sources stand.

steps.title: Why does sinking venom matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical law follows from the fact that a young snake's venom sinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A young snake's venom sinks.' For what law does this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical point of 'sinking' venom. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to know why it matters that the poison sinks. The answer will show it affects whether the rest of a drink is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? (what practical difference does it make)

phrases.english: "That of a young snake sinks":
for what law does this matter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to step 15 to ask for the practical use of 'sinking' venom.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical law that follows from venom sinking.

steps.title: The uncovered barrel: nine drank, the tenth died
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that an uncovered barrel stays forbidden even after nine people drank safely, and a story shows a tenth person dying. רבי ירמיה explains this as sinking venom.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If a barrel was left uncovered, even if nine people drank from it and did not die, a tenth should not drink from it. There was once a case where nine drank and did not die, and a tenth drank and died. רבי ירמיה said: This is sinking venom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. Because venom can sink, the lower part of an uncovered barrel can still be deadly even after others drank safely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think nine safe drinkers prove the barrel is fine. But if the venom sank, it is waiting at the bottom, and only someone who drinks later reaches it. The story proves this really happens.

keyTerms.meaning: There was an incident (a story that backs up the rule)

steps.whatToRemember: Safe results from earlier drinkers do not make an uncovered drink safe, because sinking venom may still be lower down.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think nine people drinking safely 'proves' the barrel is fine. The whole point is that the danger may only be at the bottom.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
A barrel that was left uncovered,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, which fits the feminine word for barrel.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשָּׁתוּ מִמֶּנָּה תִּשְׁעָה וְלֹא מֵתוּ —
phrases.english: even though nine people drank from it and did not die,
a tenth should not drink from it.

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה הָיָה שֶׁשָּׁתוּ מִמֶּנּוּ תִּשְׁעָה וְלֹא מֵתוּ,
phrases.english: There was an incident in which nine drank from it and did not die,
and a tenth drank and died.
Rabbi Yirmeya said: This is the sinking venom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sinking venom explains why an uncovered barrel stays forbidden even after nine people drank safely.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that in matters of danger, a 'track record' of safety does not make something permitted.

steps.title: The uncovered melon: same rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא applies the same rule to an uncovered melon, backs it with a similar story, and רבי calls it sinking venom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, if a melon was left uncovered, even if nine people ate from it and did not die, a tenth should not eat from it. There was once a case where nine ate and did not die, and a tenth ate and died. רבי said: This is sinking venom.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second example, a melon, to show the same danger applies to food and not just drink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A snake can bite into a melon and leave venom that seeps deep inside. People eating the outer parts are fine, while someone who reaches the inner part may die. So the whole melon stays forbidden.

phrases.english: And similarly, a melon that was left uncovered,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָכְלוּ מִמֶּנָּה תִּשְׁעָה בְּנֵי אָדָם
phrases.english: even though nine people ate from it
and did not die,
a tenth should not eat from it.

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה הָיָה וְאָכְלוּ מִמֶּנָּה תִּשְׁעָה וְלֹא מֵתוּ,
phrases.english: There was an incident in which nine ate from it and did not die,
and a tenth ate and died.
Rabbi said: This is the sinking venom.
phrases.notes: "רבי" on its own means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a parallel case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sinking-venom rule applies to food too: an uncovered melon stays forbidden even after nine people ate safely.

steps.title: Uncovered water may not be used at all
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids using uncovered water in any way: pouring it in public, sprinkling the floor, kneading clay, giving it to animals, or washing with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Water that was left uncovered should not be poured out in a public area, sprinkled on a house floor, used to knead clay, given to one's own animal or a friend's animal to drink, or used to wash one's face, hands, and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא teaches that uncovered water is dangerous for many uses, not just for drinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the water may hold venom, it can harm people even without being drunk. Pouring it in public could hurt someone who steps in it, clay or a sprinkled floor could carry it to bare skin, animals could die, and washing brings it onto the body.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkle water on the floor to settle dust

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Water that was left uncovered,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִשְׁפְּכֵם בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
phrases.english: one should not pour it out in a public area,
and should not sprinkle the house with it,
and should not knead clay with it,
and should not give it to drink, not to his own animal
and not to his friend's animal,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יִרְחַץ בָּהֶן פָּנָיו יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו.
phrases.english: and should not wash his face, hands, and feet with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from eating and drinking to other uses of uncovered water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Uncovered water may not be used for pouring in public, sprinkling, kneading clay, watering animals, or washing.

steps.title: אחרים: washing is forbidden only where there is a crack
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say washing with uncovered water is forbidden only on a body part with a crack or cut, and allowed where there is none.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: On a part of the body that has a crack, it is forbidden. Where there is no crack, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion, אחרים, narrows the washing ban in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Venom only harms the body if it can get inside. Where the skin has a crack or cut the venom can enter, so washing there is forbidden. On whole skin it cannot get in, so אחרים permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: Others say (a different opinion in the ברייתא)
A crack or scratch in the skin

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא forbids washing the face, hands and feet with uncovered water. אחרים forbid it only where the skin has a crack the venom could enter.

phrases.english: Others say:
a place on the body that has a crack is forbidden,
where there is no crack, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ סִירְטָא אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ברייתא's full ban on washing and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing with uncovered water is forbidden only on a body part with a crack. Otherwise it is permitted.

steps.title: Aren't אחרים saying the same thing as the תנא קמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges that the opinion of אחרים seems identical to the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The opinion of אחרים is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that אחרים (step 22) seem to say nothing new compared to the תנא קמא (step 21).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbade washing the face, hands and feet with uncovered water. אחרים forbade washing only where there is a crack or cut. Face, hands and feet are full of cracks and creases, so both opinions seem to forbid the same body parts.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', an unnamed תנא whose view is quoted in a ברייתא
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: The 'Others' are the same as the first Tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether step 22 adds anything beyond step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion of אחרים in step 22
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both opinions forbid the same body parts, there is no real disagreement.

steps.title: They differ about smooth spots on the hand, foot and face
steps.stepSummary: The difference is the back of the hand, the back of the foot, and the cheekbone area of the face.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: the back of the hand, the back of the foot, and the upper part of the face.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions really do disagree, about smooth areas that have no cracks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbids washing the whole face, hands and feet, including their smooth parts. אחרים go by cracks, so they allow washing smooth spots like the back of the hand or foot and the cheekbones.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There is a difference between them', meaning a practical case where the two opinions rule differently
The upper part of the face, the cheekbones

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא forbids the whole face, hands and feet. אחרים forbid only spots with cracks, so smooth spots are allowed.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
the back of the hand and the back of the foot
and the upper part of the face.
phrases.notes: Literally 'the pomegranates of the face', meaning the rounded cheekbones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a practical difference between the opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both opinions forbid exactly the same body parts.
steps.terutzMaskana: They disagree about smooth spots that have no cracks.

steps.title: Contradiction about giving uncovered water to one's own animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא forbids giving uncovered water to any animal, but another ברייתא allows giving it to one's own animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: He should not give it to drink to his animal or to his friend's animal. But it was taught: He may give it to his own animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes part of the ברייתא from step 21 and points out that another ברייתא seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא forbids giving uncovered water even to one's own animal. A second ברייתא explicitly allows it for one's own animal. The two sources clash, and an answer is needed.

phrases.english: The Master said:
He should not give from it to drink, not to his animal
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the ברייתא in step 21; 'it' is the uncovered water.

phrases.english: and not to his friend's animal.
But wasn't it taught:
But he may give it to drink to his own animal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of step 21 and raises a new contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that one may not give uncovered water to his own animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא explicitly allows giving it to one's own animal.

steps.title: The lenient ברייתא is talking about a cat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that allows it is talking about a cat.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about a cat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by saying the lenient ברייתא is only about a cat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Snake venom does not kill a cat the way it can kill other animals, so giving the water to one's own cat is allowed. The strict ברייתא is about other animals, which would really be in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When that one was taught', which limits a source to a specific case

phrases.english: When that one was taught, it was about a cat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting one source to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות are about every kind of animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient ברייתא is only about a cat.

steps.title: Then let him give it to his friend's cat too
steps.stepSummary: If a cat is not harmed, why not give the water to another person's cat as well?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then his friend's cat too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer: if the cat is safe, a friend's cat should be allowed too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lenient ברייתא allowed only 'his own animal'. If the reason is that cats are safe, there seems to be no reason to tell apart one's own cat and a friend's cat.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so', which brings a challenge that follows from the last answer

phrases.english: If so, his friend's [cat] too?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the cat answer of step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: Limiting the permission to one's own cat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If cats are safe, the owner should not make a difference.

steps.title: The venom weakens the friend's cat
steps.stepSummary: The venom weakens the friend's cat, so it would be causing him damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: His friend's cat gets weakened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the venom does weaken a cat, so a person may not do this to someone else's cat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cat survives the venom but becomes weak. Weakening another person's animal causes him a loss.

phrases.english: His friend's [cat] gets weakened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing out a harm to someone else
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A cat is not affected at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: A cat becomes weakened, which is a loss to its owner.

steps.title: His own cat gets weakened too
steps.stepSummary: Doesn't his own cat also get weakened?
steps.simpleTranslation: His own cat also gets weakened?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why weakening his own cat is allowed, if it is equally weakened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If weakening is the problem, it applies to one's own cat as well. So the line between one's own cat and a friend's cat is still unexplained.

phrases.english: His own [cat] also gets weakened?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 28.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Weakening happens to his own cat too, so why is that allowed?

steps.title: The cat recovers afterward
steps.stepSummary: The cat becomes healthy again later.
steps.simpleTranslation: It becomes healthy again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the weakness passes and the cat recovers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the weakness is only temporary, a person may let it happen to his own cat.

phrases.english: It becomes healthy again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The weakening is a lasting harm.

steps.title: The friend's cat also recovers
steps.stepSummary: The friend's cat would also recover, so why is it forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: His friend's cat also becomes healthy again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer around: if cats recover, the friend's cat recovers too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Recovery happens to both cats. So the difference between one's own cat and a friend's cat still needs a reason.

phrases.english: His friend's [cat] also becomes healthy again!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 30.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Recovery applies equally to the friend's cat.

steps.title: The friend may want to sell it while it is weak
steps.stepSummary: The friend may want to sell the cat while it is weak and lose money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes he wants to sell it, and he loses money from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer: the friend might need to sell the cat during its weak period and get a lower price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a temporary weakness can cause a real loss if the owner sells at that moment. With one's own cat, the owner can choose to wait. With someone else's cat, he would be risking another person's money.
steps.whatToRemember: Uncovered water may be given to one's own cat but not to someone else's, because the weakened cat could lose value if the owner sells it.

phrases.english: Sometimes he wants to sell it,
and it causes him a loss from it.
phrases.notes: Since the cat looks weak right then, it sells for less.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 31 and closes the discussion about the cat.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing out a possible financial loss
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the cat recovers, there is no loss at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: A sale during the weak period causes a real loss to the friend.

steps.title: Three kinds of wine, starting with libation wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא lists three kinds of wine. The first, יין נסך, is forbidden for any benefit and gives severe טומאה in the amount of a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי יהודה בן בתירא: There are three kinds of wine. Libation wine is forbidden to benefit from, and it makes things impure with severe impurity in an olive-sized amount.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins: a list of three kinds of wine. Here the גמרא gives the first one, יין נסך, and the other two come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יין נסך is wine actually poured for עבודה זרה. It gets the strictest treatment: a person may not get any benefit from it at all. It also gives severe טומאה, like that of עבודה זרה itself, from just a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine poured as an offering to עבודה זרה
Forbidden to get any benefit from, not just forbidden to drink
The size of an olive, a standard minimum amount

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the first of the three wines. The other two kinds, which are less strict, come right after.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira:
There are three kinds of wine:
Libation wine is forbidden for benefit,
and it makes things impure with severe impurity in an olive-sized amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of uncovered liquids ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יין נסך is forbidden for any benefit and gives severe טומאה in the amount of a כזית.
